answer: Persistent workload ledger ties each identity to sustained useful output, never to a single proof. An agent earns routing priority through a rolling record of verified tasks, so reputation accrues only where real work lands, like a vein of opal forming under pressure. At the nadir of a fresh identity, throughput is throttled until history accumulates, forcing a clone to redo the full expensive ramp. Because capacity scales with logged effort, buying many new identities yields near-zero privilege, while honest continuation costs far less than reconstructing history from quartz.
